Third, open System Configuration (msconfig) or Services and toggle off non-essential services. Check only the boxes you understand; if it sounds like a printer spooler or a telemetry helper, it’s fine to leave unchecked.

Fourth, clear your browser cache and extensions. Chrome’s settings let you delete weeks of history and remove add-ons that silently drain RAM.

Fifth, run the Disk Cleanup wizard as admin and check the "Previous Windows installations" box if you see it—those gigabytes are gone forever once you hit OK.

If you’re still tight on space, compress the Recycle Bin and the Downloads folder. Windows lets you right-click a folder, choose Properties, and tick "Compress contents to save disk space." It’s transparent and reversible.
